brief.subject: Ghana's EU timber license; Kraft Heinz sells coffee unit
brief.headline: Ghana's EU Timber License Takes Shape as Kraft Heinz Exits Coffee
brief.dek: Ghana's long VPA process with the EU yields a timber sales license, and Kraft Heinz agrees a $650 million North American coffee sale.
brief.lede: Ghana now has a license to sell sustainable timber after a 16-year Voluntary Partnership Agreement (VPA) process with the EU, a milestone for wood traders focused on legality.

sections.heading: Ghana's Timber License After 16 Years
bullets: Ghana completed a 16-year VPA process with the EU and now holds a license to sell sustainable timber.
Europe is a key market for Ghanaian timber, so the license matters directly to exporters shipping wood there.
The VPA offered Ghana both EU market access and support for stronger national forest governance.
Mongabay's analysis says the process improved institutions and cooperation, useful context for buyers assessing legality risk.

sections.heading: Kraft Heinz Sells North American Coffee
bullets: Kraft Heinz will sell its North American coffee business to One Rock for $650 million.
Kraft Heinz will keep a 30% stake, so it remains tied to the business.
Cash from the sale will go toward cutting debt.
A new majority owner may mean new contacts and supplier expectations for coffee exporters selling into this business.
